newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle calls mixed, feeders steady to up.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle calls mixed, feeders steady to up.

text.p: CME live cattle futures calls ranged from 0.100 cent lower to 0.100 higher while feeder cattle were expected to open steady to 0.200 cent higher, livestock analysts said.

Live cattle futures may trade uneven following the mixed trend in boxed beef values late Friday and expected slow fed cattle trade. Packer bids and feedlot asking prices were running $2 to $3 per cwt apart and little cash trade is seen, analysts said.
Weather had turned warmer but cattle needed time to regain weight after poor conditions the past two weeks, they said.
Trading may be influenced at times by early estimates for the monthly USDA Cattle-on-Feed report scheduled to be released Friday, they added.

Early analyst estimates on the report pointed to on-feed supplies at between 102 to 105 percent of a year ago. Placement estimates were running at 103 to 112 percent and marketing estimates at 99 to 107.1 percent of last year.
Feeder cattle were expected to continue moving higher after posting some new contract highs last week. A higher index and calls for lower corn futures should keep the market supported, analysts said.
Feeder supplies were expected to remain fairly tight and tighten even further by the fall following recent very poor weather conditions in cow/calf producing areas, they said.
The latest CME feeder cattle index was up $0.05 at $68.61 per cwt, the highest price level since March 20, 1995.
Futures will close early at noon CST in observance of the Martin Luther King Jr. holiday.
